clue.text: Oil company going about work on well, rapidly moving body of rock and ice

definitions.text: rapidly moving body of rock and ice

indicators.note: the oil-and-work piece sits on, that is follows, the word for well

parts.note: hale means healthy or well, as in hale and hearty

indicators.note: the oil company's letters go round the work, surrounding it

parts.note: BP is the British oil giant
OP is the usual abbreviation of opus, a work

explanation.surface: A news item about an oil firm drilling a well, oddly drifting into astronomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' looks like a place to drill for oil, but it is the adjective meaning healthy; 'going about' and 'on' are the container and placing signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Hale-Bopp was the bright comet of 1997, and a comet is a fast-travelling lump of rock and ice.

clue.text: Leads on hi-fi are fiddly to handle

indicators.note: the leads are the leading or first letters of each of these words

explanation.surface: The cables on a stereo are awkward to deal with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leads' suggests cables, but it takes the first letter of each word.
explanation.definitionFit: A haft is the grip of a knife, axe or tool.

clue.text: Where you'll find Ukrainians mostly live long after fifty

indicators.note: after places the shortened cheer behind fifty

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: the last letter is cut so most of the word stays

parts.note: viva is the Italian for long live

explanation.surface: Ukrainians mainly living to a great age once past fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts VIVA to VIV.
explanation.definitionFit: Lviv is a large city in western Ukraine, so a home for many Ukrainians.

clue.text: Architectural feature home had in Barking

indicators.note: in tells us the home-and-had piece is placed inside the barking

parts.note: bow-wow is the sound of a dog barking
in means at home
'd is the short form of had, as in I'd

explanation.surface: A building detail that a house in the London district of Barking possessed.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is an area of east London, so it looks like a place, not a dog's noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A bow window is a curved bay projecting from a wall, a typical building design element.

clue.text: Profile parts as unusual material for cast

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters are put in a strange new order

explanation.surface: A side view revealing odd sections of a substance used for casts.
explanation.definitionFit: This white powder mixed with water sets hard, so it is used to make casts for broken limbs and sculptures.

clue.text: Complaint associated with flying buttress

parts.note: a beef is a grumble or complaint
up means airborne, as of a plane that is flying

explanation.surface: An architectural grievance about a flying buttress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying buttress' looks like one architectural term, but the clue splits it: 'flying' is wordplay and 'buttress' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To buttress an argument or structure is to strengthen it, the same as reinforcing it.

clue.text: High spot of year in Ireland heading north

indicators.note: the year's letter goes inside the word for Ireland
in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: The best time of year in Ireland as travel heads north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading north' turns EIRE into ERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is an eagle's nest built on a cliff or high crag, so a lofty spot.

clue.text: Boxers race with teams in boats

parts.note: to fly is to race along at speed
eights are rowing crews of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: A rowing regatta with crews racing in boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxers' could be dogs or shorts, but it means fighters in a weight division.
explanation.definitionFit: Flyweight is one of the lightest boxing classes, so these are fighters in it.

clue.text: Not using present to mark courtship by mail?

definitions.meaning: dating a cheque or letter with a later day than today's
romance conducted through letters, read whimsically as dating by post

explanation.surface: Choosing old-fashioned letters rather than gifts to woo someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift but means today's date.
explanation.definitionFit: Postdating a cheque marks it with a later date than the current one.

clue.text: Kate Winslet and he played card game on TV

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are toyed with and moved about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
K stands for king, a playing card

explanation.surface: An actress and a man playing a hand of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card game' looks like one phrase, but 'card' gives K and 'game on TV' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a BBC quiz show hosted by Anne Robinson, where contestants voted each other off.

clue.text: Flying with one, the RAF are likely to take off in adverse conditions

definitions.text: likely to take off in adverse conditions

indicators.note: flying suggests letters tossed about in the air and landing in a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pilots of the Royal Air Force taking off in bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests aircraft taking off, but 'take off' means running away: a fair-weather friend deserts you when trouble comes.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair-weather friend is loyal only in good times and leaves once difficulties arise.

clue.text: Agreed viewers need no introduction

indicators.note: the word for viewers loses its opening letter, so it has no introduction

parts.note: eyes are the organs we view with, so viewers

explanation.surface: A television show whose audience already knows the presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'need no introduction' drops the first letter of EYES.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying yes is giving assent, so a single word meaning agreed or okay.

clue.text: Sat with Sun when away with Congress much of the time?

definitions.text: Sat with Sun when away with Congress much of the time?

parts.words: Sat with Sun when away with Congress much of the time?
parts.note: Saturday and Sunday spent away from home, with congress in its sense of sexual intercourse taking up most of the hours

explanation.surface: Someone sitting in the sun on a trip with a political body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sat' and 'Sun' look like a verb and the sun but are the days, and 'Congress' is lovemaking, not the US legislature.
explanation.definitionFit: A saucy weekend away is a couple's trip taken mainly for sex.

clue.text: Fictional storyteller's article culled from Obscure Birds

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: culled means removed, so the article is taken out

parts.note: obscure means unclear
a is the indefinite article
emus are large flightless Australian birds

explanation.surface: A writer's tale taken from a book of rare birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'culled from' removes an A from UNCLEAR, leaving UNCLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Joel Chandler Harris's narrator tells the Br'er Rabbit tales, so he is an invented teller of stories.

clue.text: Uncertain if fluids be suitable for pouring

indicators.note: uncertain suggests the letters are unsettled and take a new order

explanation.surface: Doubts over whether liquids are fit to be poured.
explanation.definitionFit: Something diffusible can spread out or be poured out widely, like a liquid dispersing.

clue.text: Fabulous spring being in Paris and retaining every second!

indicators.note: only every other letter of the words is kept, starting from the second

explanation.surface: A mythical creature visiting the French capital and holding on to every moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Fabulous means of fable, mythical. The second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters of 'in Paris and' are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a naiad is a nymph who lives in a spring, river or lake.

clue.text: Whereby vehicle may be seen on land, crossing river

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: the word for land goes across, straddling, the river's letter

parts.note: to alight is to come down and land

explanation.surface: A vehicle spotted on the ground as it goes over a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is the crossword's usual RE (concerning), not a position word; 'crossing' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The red lamp at the back of a car lets traffic behind see it in the dark.

clue.text: Be ready to surprise with spoonerised reason for being home after hours

indicators.note: named for Rev Spooner, it tells us the opening sounds of two words are swapped

parts.note: why asks for the reason
in means at home
late means after the usual hours

explanation.surface: An ambush explained by someone getting home late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Why in late?' is the question asked of someone home after hours; swapping the W and L sounds gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie in wait is to hide ready to ambush someone.

clue.text: Fines imposed on airline once raiding dodgy fuel serving foreign planes

indicators.note: the airline-and-fines piece breaks into the rearranged fuel, as raiders burst in
dodgy means unreliable or faulty, telling us to rearrange these letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the fines' letters are placed on the airline, following it

parts.note: TWA, Trans World Airlines, was a US carrier that no longer exists
F stands for fine on pencils, so FF is fines

explanation.surface: Penalties on a defunct airline for using bad fuel in foreign aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' makes LUFE from FUEL, and 'raiding' puts TWAFF inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Luftwaffe was the German air force, so its aircraft are planes from abroad to an English solver.

clue.text: Sort of crop said to be used for food

indicators.note: said tells us the word sounds like another when spoken

parts.note: an Eton crop is a short slicked hairstyle of the 1920s, named after the school

explanation.surface: A farmer explaining that one type of harvest goes for food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crop' suggests farming, but an Eton crop is a haircut. Eton is a famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eaten has been consumed as a meal, so it was put to use as food.

clue.text: Prize for penning university's key text

indicators.note: the prize's letters pen in, enclosing, the university

parts.note: a rosette is a ribbon award given at shows
Aston is a university in Birmingham

explanation.surface: An award for writing a crucial book at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' suggests a door key, but the stone was the key to reading hieroglyphs; 'for penning' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rosetta Stone gave scholars the key to Egyptian hieroglyphs, so it is the classic decoding inscription.

clue.text: Maybe canine's landmark birthday — extra stroke to head called for

definitions.note: the 's stands for is; a canine is one example of the thing defined

wordplay.reading: a hundredth written in figures, with a stroke topping the one to make a T

parts.words: landmark birthday — extra stroke to head
parts.note: a hundredth birthday is written 100TH, and a bar across the top of the 1 turns it into a T

explanation.surface: A dog celebrating a big birthday and asking for a pat on the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canine' suggests a dog, but it is a pointed tooth. 'called for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A canine is one of the four pointed teeth beside the incisors, so an example of the answer.

clue.text: Italian drunk and over the hill, released from physical training

indicators.note: the training letters are let go from the phrase for over the hill

parts.note: past it means too old, over the hill

explanation.surface: An old Italian, drunk, let off from gym class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'released from' removes P and T from PASTIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling wine from Piedmont in Italy, an Italian drink.

clue.text: Nick that's come away from top edge

indicators.note: the first letter breaks off the top of the word

parts.note: to nick is to steal, to pinch

explanation.surface: A notch that has broken off the upper rim of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' and 'edge' look like nouns, but nick means steal and edge means move slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge forward is to creep a little at a time, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Essential piece of information he passed on to press

indicators.note: the essential or central part of the word is its middle letter

parts.note: OB is short for Latin obiit, he died, seen on gravestones

explanation.surface: A source leaking a key fact to journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like journalists, but it is a verb meaning to crowd round.
explanation.definitionFit: To crowd eagerly around a celebrity is to throng or press about them.

clue.text: Reason for fall in grain silo when working

indicators.note: when the letters are working, set in motion, they shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Why someone tumbled inside a farm silo while on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' looks like a tumble, but it is the Fall of Man in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: In Christian teaching, Adam and Eve's first disobedience caused humanity's Fall from grace.

clue.text: To boil pudding wife's left out, light gas

indicators.note: the wife's letter is omitted from the pudding

parts.note: sweet is the British word for a dessert
W is the abbreviation for wife
He is the chemical symbol of helium, a very light gas

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions: boil the pudding, skip the wife, use gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' removes W from SWEET, giving SEET.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to bubble as if boiling, from an old verb for cooking in liquid.

clue.text: Hard to lie back after takeoff, becoming nervous

indicators.note: after places the remaining pieces behind the send-up

parts.note: a skit is a send-up or take-off

indicators.note: back tells us the hard-and-lie pair runs backwards

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
to lie or sit is to be situated, as a town sits in a valley

explanation.surface: A nervous flyer finding it hard to recline after the plane leaves the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns HSIT ('Hard' joined to SIT) into TISH. 'takeoff' looks like a plane leaving but is a comic imitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Skittish describes jumpy, easily startled behaviour, like a nervy horse.
